title: interview-live: TriggerPolicy — event-driven triggers + stale-batch drop
description:
Why: measured baseline (interview-20261113-084517, 83.5min live) shows 222 batches at median 21s producing 628 questions and forcing 587 manual dismissals (~7/min) — the human is the garbage collector. All 3 proposals converge on trigger control (claude TRG: turn end P-01 1.2s, monologue P-02 25s, coalescing; zai batcher + force key; chatgpt cadence split). This is the corrected top priority (review CORR-003 CRITICAL: measured dominant failure is flood, not topic bias).

What: pure TriggerPolicy module (utterance merge + trigger decision, injected clock) wired into the worker loop enqueue path; plus a one-line stale-drop in the suggester loop (skip batch if a newer one is queued — review EDGE-002). Keep a manual force-round path.

TDD shape — Red: policy tests (turn-end triggers, coalesce window, monologue trigger, stale-drop, no-lost-segments invariant). Green: wire worker loop. Refactor: extract policy constants (adopt claude P-01/P-02 IDs).
acceptance_criteria: suggestions trigger on guest turn end / long monologue / coalesced batch, not every 21s; queued batches dropped when newer pending; zero transcript segments lost (test-proven); median batch cadence rises vs 21s baseline
notes: New module interview_live_trigger.py must carry the repo file-header convention (Purpose/Responsibilities/Rationale) — see existing bin/interview_live_core.py header. Meter: python3 -m pytest tests/test_interview_live.py -k trigger
close_reason: TriggerPolicy shipped (uncommitted): bin/interview_live_trigger.py + loop wiring + stale-drop carry; 7 new trigger tests, 69 interview-live tests pass, 137 repo-wide (12 pre-existing test_terapia fixture errors = canticos-0cd). Integration proof: 8 triggers -> 2 pi calls, zero transcript lines lost. Live cadence re-measurement vs the 21s baseline still pending a real session.

title: interview-live: ExpiryPolicy — freshness decay + auto-expire for pending questions
description:
Why: baseline left 41 evergreen pending items in a 628-item backlog; nothing retires (claude EXP G3 with P-13 60s half-life / P-14 0.15 threshold; zai 0.94/min decay + ~8min expiry; chatgpt lifecycle states).

What: pure decay+expiry functions over question dicts (created_at / last_shown based), applied at rank/render time; expiry emits an event using the T2 vocabulary; re-entry suppressed for asked/dismissed items.

TDD shape — Red: synthetic queue expiry-ordering tests; asked-never-resurfaces test. Green: rank integration. Refactor: parameterize half-life/threshold with claude P-13/P-14 IDs.
acceptance_criteria: pending questions decay and auto-expire (bounded pending count); asked/dismissed never resurface; expiry-ordering pure-core tests; queue.json gains decay fields tolerantly
notes:
Anti-goal: do not expire pending questions that received fresh evidence inside the window — decay acts on staleness, not on existence. Anti-goal: do not tune the half-life to force a target pending count. Meter: python3 -m pytest tests/test_interview_live.py -k expiry
Orchestrator decisions: pure functions in core — decay_weight(last_seen, now, half_life=P-13 60s) = 0.5 ** (age/half_life); EXPIRY_THRESHOLD=P-14 0.15; expire at rank/render time when weight < threshold and the question is still pending, marking status='expired' and emitting question_dismissed with reason='expired' via the vvc emitter; fresh evidence (last_seen/mentions update) resets the decay. Asked/dismissed/expired never re-enter pending ranks. queue.json gains decay_weight + expires_at tolerantly. Half-life/threshold injectable, no tuning to hit a pending count.
close_reason: Implemented + tested: 94 targeted tests green (queue/tui/interview_live)

title: interview-live: question lifecycle events (question_shown/asked/dismissed)
description:
Why: all 3 proposals define an acted-on ratio (asked+dismissed over shown) and NEXT-card dwell metrics; today TUI actions leave no event trail — the baseline session (interview-20261113-084517) recorded 587 dismissals with only a final queue.json to show for it (review EDGE-004).

What: emit question_shown when a question enters the rendered view, question_asked / question_dismissed on mark_asked and the future dismiss key. Vocabulary follows the events module convention (ts/seq/typed).

TDD shape — Red: fake-pi TUI round produces shown+asked events. Green: emit sites in TUI + core hooks. Refactor: shared emit helper.
acceptance_criteria: acted-on ratio derivable from events.jsonl alone; new event types emitted on queue state transitions; no TUI behavior change yet
close_reason: Lifecycle events shipped at commit (question_shown/asked/dismissed, idempotent transitions, injectable sink); 94 interview-live tests pass on orchestrator gate.

title: interview-live: log input_lines + raw model output in suggest_result events
description:
Why: the 3 improvement proposals (zai Core v2 PDF, claude v2 spec, chatgpt spec) all define health metrics that need prompt/context attribution; today suggest_result only logs parsed questions+topics (bin/interview-live:206-209), so prompt-vs-context failure causes are unmeasurable (review EDGE-004; claude's original ask was to quantify prompt vs structural issues).

What: extend the suggest_result emit payload with input_lines (the joined new lines sent to pi) and raw_output (pi stdout before parsing). Disk cost ~1 extra KB/batch is acceptable.

TDD shape — Red: test asserts payload fields present on a fake-pi round. Green: minimal emit change in coordinator suggest(). Refactor: keep payload flat for jq-ability.
acceptance_criteria: events.jsonl suggest_result carries input_lines and raw_output on every batch; existing tests extended; no suggestion behavior change
close_reason: suggest_result now emits input_lines + raw_output (flat strings); red-first test added

title: docs: apply README front-door standard v0.4 (§5.1)
description:
Standard (authoritative, recommended (not ddl-managed)): https://github.com/charly-vibes/dulce-de-leche/blob/main/docs/standardization.md#51-readme-front-door-contract

Audit (2026-11-15): 4/10. Script table and install, but most scripts have no example.

Repo-specific gaps:
- No per-script quickstart (e.g. `interview-live`, `terapia`, `to-projector`) with expected output.
- No 'which script when' guidance; several scripts are personal workflow wrappers.
- No FAQ for dependencies, output paths, or the symlink installer.

Required changes:
- [ ] Add `## When to use` with use bullets, 'use <sibling> instead' bullets, and the assumption the tool makes.
- [ ] Make `## Quick start` install → first meaningful command → expected output.
- [ ] Add `## FAQ` (5–7 questions) or link `docs/src/faq.md` / `docs/src/troubleshooting.md` from the README first screen.
- [ ] Move repository-development recipes (`just …`, build-from-source) to `## Development`.
- [ ] Fix broken relative README links (if any).

Acceptance: §5.1 checklist passes; every documented command exists in `--help`; no broken relative links.

Release note: §1 now requires prebuilt binaries on GitHub Releases for binary tools (five targets + checksums.txt); non-binary repos record the deviation in `docs/src/status.md`.

Context: fleet README audit 2026-11-15 (45 repos); umbrella epic `charly-o1j`.

title: interview-live: replay metrics CLI — health report from events.jsonl
description:
Why: all 3 proposals define health metrics; the v2 spec requires tuning parameters by replay before treating them as fixed (17 params), and the repo now has real sessions (interview-20261113-084517 = the baseline: 5% topic-only, 628 questions, 587 dismissals). Measurement must be repeatable, not a one-off python heredoc.

What: bin/interview-live-metrics (or --metrics flag): read events.jsonl (+queue.json) and print — questions:topics ratio per batch and shown (target >= 1.0), topic-only batch %, questions/min, median cadence, acted-on ratio (needs T2 events), repair rate (needs T6 events), time-to-first-question, over-contract batch count. Human output + --json. This replaces the full deterministic-reducer Replay CLI for now (claude TEL-2/3/5 stays deferred as T15).

TDD shape — Red: golden-file test on the 20261113 session fixture (small slice). Green: metric functions pure over event dicts. Refactor: metric constants/targets from claude section 10 gates re-tuned to baseline. Blocked by T1+T2 (payloads it consumes).
acceptance_criteria: metrics CLI prints Q:T ratio, topic-only %, questions/min, cadence, acted-on, repair rate, time-to-first-question; --json mode; golden-file test on 20261113 fixture slice
notes:
Note (DEP-002): repair rate prints 'n/a (no suggest_reject events)' until canticos-ap3 lands; metrics CLI is NOT blocked by ap3 to avoid serialization.
New module bin/interview_live_metrics.py must carry the repo file-header convention. Meter: python3 -m pytest tests/test_interview_live.py -k metrics && bin/interview_live_metrics.py ~/Interviews/interview-20261113-084517/events.jsonl (golden baseline: topic-only 5.4%, 628 questions, 222 batches).
close_reason: Metrics CLI committed a57f8f7; 6 tests + CLI output verified.

title: interview-live: stateless prompt digest — full contract+window+pending every round
description:
Why: the system prompt is only sent on the first round; later rounds are bare delta-lines into a growing pi session (build_pi_cmd, suggest.py — zai PDF root cause RC-2, verified at HEAD). The methodology and JSON contract decay as the session grows; session cost creeps. claude PRM (stateless byte-budgeted prompt, P-03 12k) and zai (state digest; PDF open question: stateless questioner / sessioned detector) converge; decision on record: stateless questioner.

What: every round sends a full prompt — rolling window (last ~40 lines), new lines since last batch, pending-question digest (post-T4: decayed/expired-aware), and the MOM_SYSTEM_PROMPT contract. Retire --session-id continuity for suggestions (pi session stays for debugging only if cheap).

TDD shape — Red: prompt builder includes window+digest+contract every round; byte budget respected. Green: swap build_pi_cmd path. Refactor: PromptBuilder module per claude component map. Blocked by T4 (digest needs decayed pending set).
acceptance_criteria: every suggestion round carries system prompt + rolling window + pending digest within byte budget; pi session continuity no longer required for suggestion quality
notes: Orchestrator decisions: stateless questioner per claude PRM — every round sends system prompt + rolling window (last 40 transcript lines) + new lines since last batch + pending-question digest. Byte budget P-03 = 12000 chars total prompt; trim window first, then digest, never the contract. Drop --session-id for suggestion calls (pi session kept only for debugging); build_pi_cmd keeps a stateless path selected by default with tests asserting the system prompt is present on every call.
close_reason: Stateless prompt: contract+window+new lines+pending digest every round, 12k budget, --session-id retired for suggestions. Committed 1d83093; 137 tests pass.

title: interview-live: NEXT-card TUI — ASK NOW lead card, backlog, dismiss/select keys
description:
Why: the TUI renders one mixed ranked backlog; the baseline session shows what that costs — 587 space-presses (one every ~8.5s for 83 minutes) because the interviewer must triage a flood. All 3 proposals converge on the NEXT-card/ASK NOW pattern (claude UX group; zai hybrid priority lead card; chatgpt ASK NOW top-3).

What: three-zone queue pane — ASK NOW lead card (best pending question + grounds quote + [MM:SS], stable for a minimum dwell P-16 8s, hysteresis P-11 0.10), compact backlog of 3-5 with j/k selection, topics demoted per T10. Keys: a/space = ask selected, d = dismiss (removes v1 d-as-PgDn alias — keep PgDn working and show a one-session hint; review EDGE-005), j/k select, q quit. Dismissal is negative feedback: emits question_dismissed (T2) and feeds the ranker. Plain stdout mode keeps parity (lead card + quote + backlog per round).

TDD shape — Red: pure build_layout() tests for the three zones, truncation at 52 cols, dwell/hysteresis stability; key-handler tests via stubbed ui state. Green: curses + plain modes. Refactor: layout constants. Blocked by T2 (lifecycle events), T3 (trigger — without it the card churns), T4 (expiry — without it the card rots).
acceptance_criteria: three-zone layout; lead card stable (dwell + hysteresis); a/space ask, d dismiss (emits event, feeds ranker), j/k select; plain-mode parity; PgDn keeps working
notes: Orchestrator decisions: ASK NOW lead card = highest-score pending question, stable for min dwell P-16 = 8s and only replaced when a challenger beats it by hysteresis P-11 = 0.10; backlog shows 3-5 following pending questions with j/k selection (selected index default 0); keys: a/space ask selected, d dismiss selected (emits question_dismissed), j/k move selection, PgDn keeps scrolling transcript for one more session with a footer hint, q quits. Plain stdout prints lead card + grounds/quote + [MM:SS] + 3-item backlog per batch. Layout stays pure build_layout(ui, w, h, scroll, now) with lead/backlog zones.
close_reason: Three-zone NEXT card (lead dwell 8s/hysteresis 0.10, backlog 3-5, j/k/a/space/d keys, PgDn retained, plain parity) committed; 146 interview-live tests pass.

title: interview-live: contract hardening — validate_round + grounds fuzzy-match + one repair round
description:
Why: the output contract still silently accepts zero-question batches (parse_suggestion_output returns ([], topics) with no warning) and question grounding lives only inside the question text with no verification. Measured at HEAD the contract mostly holds (12/222 = 5% topic-only, 4/222 over the 2-4 shape) so this is now SECOND priority (review CORR-003), targeting the 5% residue plus hallucinated-grounds prevention before it can appear.

What (zai Core v2 move 1 + claude PRM/LLM groups): validate_round() enforcing — at least 1 question per batch; questions as objects with a grounds quote fuzzy-matched against the recent transcript window (es morphology: light suffix stripping, shared with the dedupe normalizer); >2 topics flagged; plain-line fallback counted as a contract miss. Exactly ONE repair round on failure (same model+inputs plus the rejected output quoted), then a suggest_reject event; repair inherits the stale-guard. New events: suggest_reject, suggest_repair. Needs T1 (raw payload) and T2 vocabulary.

TDD shape — Red: parser rejects empty-questions batch; repair invoked once then logged; grounds fuzzy-match verified against fake transcript window (es fixtures); hallucinated quote demoted not deleted. Green: coordinator repair path. Refactor: validator constants.
acceptance_criteria: zero-question batches trigger exactly one repair round then suggest_reject; grounds fuzzy-match blocks hallucinated quotes (es fixtures); plain-line fallback counted as contract miss
notes:
Anti-goal: unverifiable-grounds questions are DEMOTED with a no-evidence mark, never silently deleted (zai behavior). Anti-goal: exactly one repair round — no retry loops. Anti-goal: plain-line fallback must keep working (counted as contract miss, not dropped). Meter: python3 -m pytest tests/test_interview_live.py -k validate
Orchestrator decisions: validate_round(questions, topics, window_lines) returns (accepted, rejected, reasons); >=1 question required; grounds quote fuzzy-matched against window via the shared es stemmer/Jaccard >= 0.7 (reuse interview_live_core.jaccard_score); unverifiable grounds => demote with evidence='no-evidence' (never delete); >2 topics => flagged only; plain-line fallback => contract_miss=True but kept. Exactly one repair round with the rejected output quoted in the prompt; then suggest_reject with reasons. Events: suggest_repair, suggest_reject.
close_reason: validate_round + grounds fuzzy-match (es stemmer, Jaccard>=0.7, demote-not-delete) + exactly one repair round with stale guard; events suggest_repair/suggest_reject. Committed 1d83093; 137 interview-live tests pass.

title: interview-live: Jaccard paraphrase dedupe with Spanish suffix stripping
description:
Why: questions currently dedupe by exact normalized text (core.py normalize_topic key), so paraphrase storms fragment the queue. Zai quick-win + claude P-07 (0.85 merge) + zai PDF (Jaccard >= 0.7) converge here; both flag Spanish morphology as the risk (suffix stripping needed).

What: token-overlap merge in Queue._ingest with a light es suffix-stripping normalization pass before tokenizing; merged items keep the latest variant text and mentions++.

TDD shape — Red: Spanish paraphrase fixture pairs merge; genuinely distinct questions survive. Green: ingest integration. Refactor: threshold constant.
acceptance_criteria: reworded repeats merge at Jaccard >= 0.7 post suffix-stripping; es paraphrase fixtures; no regression in existing dedupe tests
notes: Anti-goal: do NOT merge questions scoring below the threshold — the es distinct-question fixtures must survive. Anti-goal: do not raise the threshold to shrink the queue (that is expiry's job, not dedupe's). Meter: python3 -m pytest tests/test_interview_live.py -k dedupe
close_reason: Implemented and gated on orchestrator: wave-1 commits 89a0c9b (4pi) / c1635f0 (4zn,5rs); 76 interview-live tests pass; docs grep sweep clean.

title: interview-live: reactive TUI dashboard (participant count, live transcript, prioritized question/topic queue)
description: Turn interview-live's plain stdout loop into a reactive curses dashboard. At session start the user marks how many participants are in the conversation (count only; whisper -di stays capped at 2 speaker labels, guests share speaker 1). The TUI then shows: (a) the live rolling transcript, and (b) a prioritized queue of pi-suggested follow-up questions plus important topics, ordered so recurring/high-priority items float to the top as the interview progresses. Observe-only default: no interaction required; minimal optional keys (q quit, space mark top question asked, PgUp/PgDn scroll). TUI auto-enables on a TTY (--no-tui to force plain mode; --tui to force). Worker side: pi system prompt extended to ask for JSON {questions, topics[high|med|low]} with a tolerant fallback to legacy plain lines; new queue.json artifact (dedupe + mention counts + scores); --participants N flag feeds roster display and the pi system prompt.
design:
- tests/test_interview_live.py: PI_FAKE gains PI_MODE=json branch; new e2e tests for participants + queue.json; unit tests (in-file, importing bin/interview_live_core) for recurrence ranking and parsing fallback
- new bin/interview_live_core.py: pure Queue model (normalize/ingest/rank/snapshot) + parse_suggestion_output (JSON first, plain-line fallback); no I/O, no curses
- new bin/interview_live_tui.py: TuiState, pure build_layout() (curses-free, unit-testable), thin curses draw()/prompt_participants()/run_dashboard(); lazy curses import so plain mode never depends on ncurses
- bin/interview-live: imports core+tui (sys.path insert of script dir, symlink-safe); suggest() parses pi output into Queue, writes queue.json + questions.md (questions and topics sections); run()/run_loop refactored: worker loop appends to TuiState when ui active (no stdout writes), plain loop unchanged; _run_tui = worker thread + curses.wrapper; SIGINT handler keeps plain-mode behavior
acceptance_criteria: - new tests pass: participants forwarded to pi system prompt (3 / default 2); queue.json written with deduped topics gaining mentions across rounds and high scores ranking above low; plain pi output still lands in questions.md and works (fallback); participants 0 rejected at CLI; --no-tui/pipe mode keeps existing 9 tests green (plain stdout)

Real-pty TUI smoke passed: participants prompt (3), Guests(2) roles, priority queue pane, q quits cleanly. Code NOT committed yet (conservative beads profile).

title: interview-live: threads/slots + goal model (ThreadTracker, SlotModel, goal-gap ranking)
description:
Why: claude THR group (threads = topics with state; Mom Test discovery slots via SlotModel) and chatgpt goals[] (3-5 learning goals, goal balancing, "goal #2 untouched 15min" flag) are the deepest prioritization upgrade, but both depend on a stable stateless prompt (T8) and lifecycle (T4) to matter. Post-baseline this is phase-2 depth, not flood relief.

What: ThreadTracker + SlotModel (pluggable per interview type) + goals digest in the prompt; every question carries goal_id/thread refs; ranker includes goal-gap term (chatgpt score: goal_gap + evidence salience + recency - already_asked - age_decay).

title: interview-live: topics strip decision — demote to context strip or drop pane
description:
Why: baseline topics are near-useless as rendered: 256 topics, near-zero recurrence, names like "Cover OFF x2" and "LA CAUSALIDAD TEMPORAL REVELADA (29:48)" — meta-noise competing with actions for screen space (chatgpt UX row: backlog interpretation burden; zai demotes topics to a context strip; claude: topic cannot exist without a path to a question).

What: decide and implement — option A: one-line topics context strip (name + mentions + check once a question exists for it, zai style); option B: drop the topics pane entirely and keep topics as internal synthesizer state only. Either way topics stop rendering as ranked action items. Linked: zai topic-to-question synthesizer (2+ mentions, 0 questions) rides on this state.

TDD shape — Red: layout tests for strip/absence; synthesizer trigger test (mentions>=2, question_count=0). Green: TUI + state. Refactor: TopicState extraction. Blocked by T7.
acceptance_criteria: topics no longer render as ranked action items; synthesizer trigger (2+ mentions, 0 questions) specified and tested for the chosen option
notes:
DESIGN lane: the strip-vs-drop decision needs an interactive session (semantics decision, not AFK work); implementation of the chosen option is a separate afk ticket spun off after the decision.
Decision (2026-11-13, orchestrator): OPTION A — demote topics to a one-line context strip (name + mentions + '✓' when a question exists for the topic), keep topics as internal synthesizer state; no ranked action-item rendering. Synthesizer trigger: topic with mentions>=2 and question_count==0. Rationale: reversible, matches zai, preserves the topic->question path; dropping the pane (option B) loses signal for canticos-47b.
close_reason: Option A: topics demoted to a one-line TEMAS context strip with has-question checkmarks; deterministic synthesizer for mentions>=2 with no question (low priority, no-evidence, ranked below grounded). Committed; 246 repo tests pass.
